title: Software Engineering
description: The software process and life cycle; waterfall and V models; prototyping, phased and spiral development; agile methods and RAD and how to choose a process; requirements and modelling notations; dependability, critical systems and formal methods; and software testing, quality and maintenance. Built from the CSC 335 lecture on software process models (weeks 3 and 4); requirements, dependability, testing, quality and maintenance, which the 2021/22 paper tests but no file covers, are written from general knowledge.

topics.title: The Software Process and Life Cycle
topics.summary: A process is a series of steps involving activities, constraints and resources that produce an intended output. The software life cycle runs from requirements analysis through design, coding, testing and delivery to maintenance, and process models describe how those activities are organised.
subtopics: Meaning and characteristics of a process
Importance of processes and reasons for modelling them
Phases of the software development cycle
Requirements, design, implementation, testing, installation, maintenance
The software life cycle
List of software process models

topics.title: The Waterfall and V Models
topics.summary: The waterfall model breaks development into linear, sequential phases, each finished before the next, which suits stable, well-understood requirements. The V model bends the steps upward after coding, pairing each development phase with a testing phase.
subtopics: Characteristics of the waterfall model
When to use the waterfall model
Advantages and disadvantages of the waterfall model
Waterfall with prototyping
The V model: verification and validation
Merits and demerits of the V model

topics.title: Prototyping, Phased and Spiral Models
topics.summary: Prototyping builds a working model with limited functionality to clarify requirements early. Phased development delivers the system in pieces, incrementally or iteratively, and Boehm's spiral model repeats identification, design, construction and risk analysis in loops.
subtopics: The prototype model and its advantages and disadvantages
Incremental and iterative development
Production and development systems in parallel
The spiral model (Boehm, 1986)
Spiral phases: identification, design, construct, evaluation and risk analysis
When to use the spiral model

topics.title: Agile Methods, RAD and Choosing a Process
topics.summary: Agile methods value individuals, working software, customer collaboration and responding to change, delivering incremental builds in time boxes. RAD uses minimal planning and parallel prototypes, and the right process depends on customer involvement, requirement stability, team and experience.
subtopics: The agile manifesto
Iterations, time boxes and incremental builds
Merits and demerits of agile methods
Rapid application development
When RAD applies; its advantages and disadvantages
Factors in choosing a software process

topics.title: Requirements Engineering and Modelling Notations
topics.summary: Requirements engineering elicits, analyses, specifies and validates what a system must do, separating functional from non-functional requirements. Systems are modelled with notations such as UML use case, class, sequence, activity and state diagrams, and data flow diagrams.
subtopics: Requirements engineering activities
Functional and non-functional requirements
The requirements document
Modelling notations: UML diagrams and DFDs
Use case diagrams; include and extend
Modelling a library system

topics.title: Dependability, Critical Systems and Formal Methods
topics.summary: Critical systems are those whose failure causes serious loss, so they must be dependable: available, reliable, safe and secure, as well as repairable, maintainable, survivable and error-tolerant. Formal methods use mathematical specification and proof to build such systems.
subtopics: Safety-, mission- and business-critical systems
Dimensions of dependability: availability, reliability, safety, security
Other properties: repairability, maintainability, survivability, error tolerance
Fault avoidance, detection and tolerance
Formal methods and formal specification
Why developers use formal methods

topics.title: Software Testing, Quality and Maintenance
topics.summary: Testing shows a program does what it should and finds defects, from unit and integration testing to release and acceptance testing. Quality assurance applies principles to produce quality systems, and maintenance keeps software useful as it evolves.
subtopics: The software testing process: test cases, data, results, reports
Development, release and user testing; alpha, beta and acceptance tests
Verification and validation
Software quality assurance and quality principles
Types of maintenance: corrective, adaptive, perfective, preventive
